## Population differentiation measures

For these measures, a _gtypes_ object needs to be stratified. For example, we can use the built in example object _dloop.g_:
```{r}
dloop.g
```

For sequence data, the degree of nucleotide divergence (pairwise sequence difference) and Nei's dA can be calculated with _nucleotideDivergence()_:
```{r}
nucleotideDivergence(dloop.g)
```
This returns a list with a summary of the pairwise distances _$within_ strata and Nei's dA and pairwise distances _$between_ strata.

For standard measures of population structure (e.g., Fst, PHIst, Jost's D, etc.), there are two main functions. The first, _overallTest()_ computes the test statistic and permutation p-value for the global null hypotheses that all individuals have been drawn at random from a single population and stratification was random with respect to individual genotypes. The test will compute all statistics and their respective permutation p-values (if _nrep_ > 0). The statistics computed will be different depending on if the _gtypes_ object provided is haploid or diploid.

Here is an example for haploid sequence data:
```{r}
ovl <- overallTest(dloop.g)
ovl
```

The result is a list with the sample size (_$strata.freq_) of each stratum, and a matrix with the values of the test statistic and p-value (_$result_).

For pairwise tests, the _pairwiseTest()_ function is used:
```{r}
pws <- pairwiseTest(dloop.g)

str(pws)
```
This produces a list where each element is a unique pair of strata. The results for each pair of strata are formatted the same way as the single result from _overallTest()_.

The pairwise results can be more easily compiled into a single data.frame with _pairwiseSummary()_:
```{r}
pairwiseSummary(pws)
```
Here, there is one row for each pairwise test with a formatted _label_ column that provides the strata and sample size and then columns following the individual strata, sample sizes, test statistics, and their p-values.

For a given statistic, one use _pairwiseMatrix()_ to produce a summary matrix that gives the test statistic in the lower left and p-value in the upper right:
```{r}
pairwiseMatrix(pws, stat = 'Fst')
```

The process is exactly the same for diploid data, but other test statistics are computed:
```{r}
pws.msats <- pairwiseTest(msats.g)
pairwiseSummary(pws.msats)
```
